newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore government securities end narrowly mixed.
newsitem.headline: Singapore government securities end narrowly mixed.

text.p: Singapore government securities ended narrowly mixed in moderate trade on retail and interbank interest, dealers said on Tuesday.

"The market was narrowly mixed today amid uncertainty over market direction. Treasury bill yields were slightly higher but bond prices were slightly lower. The interbank rate was unchanged and volume was moderate," a local dealer said.

In treasury bills, three-months closed at a yield of 2.11/2.06 percent compared with Monday's yield of 1.93/1.88 percent and one-year at a yield of 1.73/1.68 percent against Monday's 1.70/1.65 percent.
Among bonds, July 1998 ended at S$99.20/99.25 from Monday's close of S$99.22/99.27, September 2001 at S$99.23/99.28 versus S$99.25/99.30 and June 2003 at S$98.75/98.80 against S$98.90/98.95.
The overnight interbank offered rate was unchanged from Monday's 2-5/8 2-1/2 percent.
